report:
Theorem 1 and the single specified FS-net consequence are established under the stated actual algebraic signature. Two harmless wording corrections are needed: FS must mean the full, generically finite section-metric class, allowing supported poles; and the assertion f_m∈FS(B) in (12) applies to degrees with H⁰(X,mB)≠0. Such degrees contain a cofinal divisibility subset, so this correction changes neither Q_B(f) nor the decreasing multiplier-ideal net. Theorem 1 remains valid in every admissible degree.

The availability argument works for every rational model obstacle. A rational model function involves finitely many invariant vertical fractional ideals. Time multiplication makes them honest ideals supported at zero. Principalizing their product on X×P¹ gives a smooth equivariant modification on which each ideal is invertible, preserving the obstacle. Functoriality under smooth morphisms makes the centers invariant: apply it to the action and projection maps from G_m×Y. At each blowup, choose a sufficiently positive linearized twist making its invariant ideal globally generated. The Rees construction embeds the blowup into a product with a projective representation; a further very ample pullback twist gives an actual linearized very ample bundle. Thus this construction imposes neither a cardinality condition nor finite generation of the section ring.

Equations (3)–(7) check exactly. Choose M≥max_E|coeff_E(D)|/b_E. Proper coherence and normality give π_*O=O: locally the pushforward is a finite algebra inside the unchanged fraction field, hence equals the integrally closed target ring. Locally trivializing the pulled-back bundle proves the required projection-formula identification. The sections of O(−mMF) and O(mMF) are respectively t^{mM}V_m[t] and t^{−mM}V_m[t]. These give precisely the two lattice bounds, including empty section spaces.

The G_m grading makes membership termwise. The increasing flag W_a therefore supplies the homogeneous adapted basis in (4), with exactly the stated weight bounds; no claim about the entire graded section ring is required. With one c>M, the twisted generator is t^{−(w_mj+mc)}s_mj. Its exponent is nonpositive at infinity. Absolute regularity permits exactly 0≤r≤w_mj+mc in (5). Linear independence of the s_mj excludes cancellation of forbidden powers at infinity, so (5) describes the FULL absolute complete system. Its restriction generates t^{−mc}Λ_m. Dividing by the actual frame t^{−mc}, equivalently multiplying the rational section by t^{mc}, preserves the coefficient ideal and proves (6) in every admissible degree. The dimension count (7) then certifies actual bigness of P, not merely numerical positivity.

The primary [DEL statements](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0002035v2) have exactly the complex, smooth, absolute projective scope claimed. Their generation coefficient is d+1. Applying them to each integral mP therefore gives C₀=K_𝓧+(n+2)H, independent of m. For rational P, an integral multiple and the cofinal common-multiple indexing identify the same asymptotic ideals.

The arbitrary-field passage is sound. One finitely generated field F₀ can contain all fixed equations, morphisms, bundles, divisor presentations, linearizations and identifications. Projectivity and very ampleness are retained by the descended embedding. Smoothness descends faithfully flatly; geometric integrality follows by passing through an algebraic closure inside k. A finite transcendence basis embeds in C and its finite algebraic extension embeds thereafter. No embedding of k is used.

Complete section spaces and their evaluation ideals commute with extensions by [flat base change](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KH). For each nonzero fixed ideal, principalization over F₀ supplies a genuine log resolution. After extension it remains smooth with geometric simple normal crossings. Components may split, but their coefficients remain unchanged; relative canonical divisors and coefficientwise floors pull back correctly. Proper flat base change consequently proves the fixed multiplier-ideal identity. Resolution independence over arbitrary fields also follows by descending any two finite resolutions and comparing their complex formulas. This avoids assuming an arbitrary-field multiplier-ideal theorem.

For each fixed m, graded multiplication gives a_q^ℓ⊂a_qℓ. A common resolution proves I_q⊂I_qℓ, including the required equality for powers and rescaled exponents. On a finite affine cover, noetherianity gives a maximum in the directed coherent-ideal family. Its extension dominates every extended member and is itself a member, hence is the extended maximum. There is no uniform stabilization degree across m and none is needed. Ideal inclusions descend faithfully flatly. The evaluation map for each descended twisted ideal has the correct base-changed H⁰ source; its cokernel vanishes after complex extension and therefore before extension. Extending to k proves generation with the SAME C₀ for every admissible m.

Open restriction of the resolution formula is exact. The restricted global maximum remains a member and dominates every restricted member, proving (11), rather than merely one inclusion. Adding rH preserves generation; sufficiently large r makes C₁ ample. Adding qF preserves both generation and ampleness because qF is globally generated. Canonical bundles, H and F carry actual linearizations. Equivariance identifies C₁ with its generic restriction over G_m, giving a vertical divisor on the affine chart. Comparing that divisor with ±NF bounds its model function. Adding qF adds q under φ_F=1, so one q makes φ_C≥0. The generic restriction C is ample.

Removing mcF by its frame gives actual relative sections of (mℬ+𝓒)b_m. The multiplier ideals are invariant, by functorial resolution and uniqueness of the asymptotic maximum. Proper pushforward over A¹ is a finite graded k[t]-module. Taking weight components of finitely many module generators gives finitely many actual homogeneous generating sections, with evaluation ideal exactly b_m.

I checked the complete [Addendum section/base-ideal proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.07183v2), specifically Lemmas 1.6–1.7 and the preceding generated-sheaf calculation. Lemma 1.5’s P-envelope comparison is unnecessary. In a local frame, the coefficient valuation of t^{−λ}s is v(s)−λ+mf. Regularity gives the section inequality at every supported semivaluation; conversely the inequalities at the normalized central-component valuations exclude all possible vertical poles, and normality gives extension. Evaluating an ideal generated by these coefficients proves the metric identity, also when every coefficient has value +∞. Products give the divisibility increase of f_m. Every rationally weighted competitor below f extends and is dominated by the corresponding complete-system stage. Real weights are obtained by downward rational approximation, using powers to clear all denominators. Thus (12) holds pointwise on the full carrier.

The same coefficient calculation for the homogeneous generators of (mℬ+𝓒)b_m proves (13) as an actual section metric on B+C/m, including its supported −∞ values. Since a_mℓ⊂b_mℓ⊂b_m^ℓ, cofinal multiples give Q_B(f)≤f+φ_bm/m. Since b_m⊂O, its ideal function is nonpositive. These prove every inequality in (14). Subadditivity gives φ_bmℓ≤ℓφ_bm; together with φ_C≥0 this proves Ψ_mℓ≤Ψ_m. Ideal valuations and these inequalities remain valid with value +∞, so no supported points are lost.

A nonzero section of an admissible multiple of B, shifted below inf f, gives a competitor finite at the generic trivial valuation. Hence inf_m Ψ_m has finite generic value. The decreasing infimum is usc, exists at every point, and its stage classes tend to c₁(B). It therefore meets the [FS-net definition of psh](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229), without a decreasing-closure theorem.

No general P_B(f) equality, relative-floor closure, compactness, Monge–Ampère equation, or original catalogue closure is established or used.
